_doc: Authored rooms stamped into the adventure's procedural floors (src/adventure/rooms.rs). 'kinds' are SiteKind names; 'floor' is any | first | last | deep (below the first). Each room has one way in on its border: D a door, d a secret door, Q a riddle door, G the gate of a lever puzzle, + a plain gap. Legend: # wall, . floor, ~ shallows, w deep water, r rubble, S sarcophagus with grave goods, C chest, * a treasure on a plinth, A altar, B brazier, P pillar, x statue, b bones, W web, T a dart trap, E an engraving (the place's history), R remains (bones that tell), p a pressure plate, o a plate marked safe, L a lever of the puzzle, M a monster of the place, h throne, k bookshelf, t table, l sconce, f fountain, c crate, a barrel. 'text' is told when one first comes into the room.

rooms.text: Black water stands knee-deep among the coffins, and something moves under it.
Skulls, thousands of them, stacked to the ceiling in patient rows.
A forgotten reliquary, sealed behind the wall. The dust has not been disturbed in centuries.
A throne built of bones and broken shields. Whoever sits it is not here. Not yet.
Three levers stand in the floor of a bare hall, and a portcullis bars a vault beyond.
A door of carved stone with a face upon it. Its lips move.
A long hall paved in great plates of stone; some bear a skull, worn smooth by feet.
Webs thick as sailcloth, and in them pale sacks that twitch.
The beast's larder: what it did not finish, and what its victims carried.
The roof came down here long ago. Under the rubble, a hand still reaches for a pick.
A dead forge of the old dwarves. The anvil is cold; the runes over it are not.
An armoury bricked up and forgotten, its racks still full.
Shelves of rotting books, and one desk where the ink is still wet.
A black altar, its stone stained. Candles burn though no one lit them.
The hall is half under water. Statues stand to their waists in it, watching.
A party of adventurers ended here. They did not end well.
Statues of the old lords, their faces chiselled away by someone who hated them.
A circle of braziers around a pit. The pit hums.
A guard room, the dice still on the table, the guards not far.
A fountain still runs here, clear and cold, under a cracked dome.
Cells, their doors rusted shut. In one, someone scratched the days on the wall until they stopped.
A smugglers' cache behind a false wall: crates, a lamp gone cold, a tally of debts.
Someone lived down here a long time, hidden from whatever hunts these tunnels.

riddles.q: I have cities but no houses, forests but no trees, water but no fish. What am I?
The more you take, the more you leave behind. What are they?
What walks on four legs at dawn, two at noon and three at dusk?
I am always hungry, I must always be fed; the finger I lick will soon turn red.
What has roots as nobody sees, is taller than trees, up, up it goes, and yet never grows?
Voiceless it cries, wingless flutters, toothless bites, mouthless mutters.
This thing all things devours: birds, beasts, trees, flowers; gnaws iron, bites steel, grinds hard stones to meal.
What can you keep after giving it to someone?
